correctness.rationale: A one-point extension over a path is exactly a ternary word avoiding three explicit pairs per old edge; Fraïssé free amalgamation gives complete nonalgebraic type realization. The two transfer matrices were reconstructed. Reversing suffix arcs and status signs yields a strictly positive factorization at every switch coordinate. Uniqueness of extrema follows by coordinatewise monotonicity; Cayley-Hamilton on the two explicit 3×3 matrices gives the exact recurrence sequences. Direct enumerations (255), switch checks (45,057), and factor checks (4,097) replayed. The all-n proof is analytic/combinatorial, not an extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Targeted published-finding corpus semantic queries, related mathematical claims, public scholarly searches, and material from the closest primary papers were compared by mathematical implication. The closest same-structure finite-base result gives a five-vertex low-arity collision, not the all-length path switch-order theorem; a directed-path result concerns the opposite forbidden tournament. Cherlin establishes free-amalgamation existence; Kuhn–Osthus–Townsend–Zhao establish global asymptotic multipartiteness, not conditional one-type path extremality. No covering statement was found. Residual transfer-matrix equivalence and inaccessible older literature leave historical priority provisional.

value.rationale: The count is a canonical invariant measuring complete local types in a natural Fraïssé limit. The result determines a strict order on all 2^(n-2) orientation-change patterns and every extremizer at every path length, and proves exponentially different complexity rates for coherent versus alternating directions. The exact suffix-factor formula gives a mechanism that a single finite list or simple transfer recurrence alone does not provide.
